name: lib/sound
description: Sound out of this machine: the device abstraction, the cross-platform OpenAL driver behind it, and the Ogg/Vorbis decoder and stream player that reach a speaker without touching the codec registry.
residual: Split out of std/media 2026-08-24. SoundDevices was the only part of that package with nothing graphical about it, and it sat behind headless: false because its neighbours decode pictures.

OpenAL + OpenALSound (g.f.) are the driver: HostLibs loads libopenal.so.1 and the device registers itself in SoundDevices.devices. Measured on Linux the day this package was written -- 'Cross-platform OpenAL sound driver', a channel at 44100Hz/16bit, and audible sound.

OGGVorbisPlayer (Christian Wassmer, ETH, April 2004) carries its own HTTP streaming and its own Vorbis decoder, so unlike MP3Decoder and WAVCodec it never imports Codecs -- which is why sound can be headless today and MP3 cannot: Codecs imports Raster and Texts.
MP3 waits for Codecs to be split into an audio half and a graphical one. AAC does not exist here at all.

Moved out of std/ 2026-08-27 by the Rust border (docs/STDLIB.md): the standard library holds what packages talk to each other through; this is a leaf that ob get can deliver. Sources still live in source/ -- only the classification moved. `headless` false keeps it out of the SDK payload.
